Subject: Key telemetry and escrow evidence request for private deployment

Ben —

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement and security at Acme are running a quick evidence pass as part of the on-prem contract review. Two asks we need to close before SOW:

1) Concrete examples of telemetry / egress logs that show key usage when Redwood runs in a customer VPC (BYOK enabled). We need to validate that key material never leaves our boundary and that any egress related to KMS interaction is auditable.

2) If Redwood supports any form of escrow for root key material (for disaster recovery), what are the controls and artifacts we can expect (attestations, signed HSM logs, key-split docs)?

Attached is our standard questionnaire (procurement side). If you can point me to a single PDF that bundles the evidence (diagram + signed logs) that would help accelerate sign-off. Happy to hop on a 30m call.

Thanks,
Alice Kim

AcmeCorp

Subject: Re: Key telemetry and escrow evidence request for private deployment

Alice —

Appreciate the clear asks. Looping in Priyom (security) and Mina (ops) to provide artifacts and a short narrative. High-level answers up front so procurement can move:

- Telemetry / egress: Redwood Private runs a customer-managed control plane inside your VPC; KMS calls are proxied through a sealed key proxy or customer HSM depending on the BYOK mode. We produce signed audit events for every key unwrap/derive operation including timestamp, VM id, caller identity, and HSM attestation nonce. Those audit lines are retained for 1 year by default and can be exported as a single bundled PDF (we'll attach).

- Escrow / recovery: We do offer an optional split-escrow model for root keys where Redwood holds an encrypted fragment and the customer holds another. Escrow only happens by explicit customer opt-in, and any release requires an agreed ceremony + signed attestation from the customer's HSM.

Priyom / Mina — can you attach: (A) a short evidence bundle (diagram + signed HSM log snippet + retention policy) and (B) the completed questionnaire where we map answers to your fields?

I'll propose a 30m sync tomorrow afternoon; what times work for you, Alice?

Best,
Ben Carter

Ben / team / Alice —

Thanks — attaching the evidence package we typically provide for BYOK private deployments. Highlights and callouts below. Attachment: escrow-telemetry-proof-v1.pdf

1) Telemetry schema (excerpt)
- event_type: KMS.UNWRAP | KMS.WRAP | KMS.DERIVE
- timestamp_utc: ISO8601
- caller_principal: service-account@example (redacted)
- instance_id: i-abc123 (customer VM id)
- hsm_attestation: base64(SIGN(nonce || event_hash))
- request_hash: sha256 of request payload (deterministic)

We sign each event at the HSM level with an attestation key. The PDF contains 3 redacted signed events showing a real unwrap (nonce included) and HSM signature verification steps.

2) Egress characterization
- For sealed-proxy BYOK: calls are TLS to customer-managed proxy within the VPC; no key material leaves the VPC. Only signed attestations (small base64 signatures) cross the boundary to Redwood's control plane for audit indexing.
- For direct HSM integration: Redwood does not receive key material — we receive only HSM-signed attestations and operation metadata.

3) Escrow model (optional)
- Split-escrow: 2-of-3 split where customer holds two fragments or a customer+third-party witness model.
- Release requires: documented change request, two operator approvals (customer + Redwood), and an HSM-signed nonce proving key reconstruction.
- We can provide notarized ceremony logs (signed by HSM) as part of the escrow package.

4) Rotation & TTL
- Recommended rotation cadence: wrapping key rotation quarterly, master root wrap every 12 months (customer-configurable).
- Operators must record rotation steps in the ceremony log; we ingest the signed rotation statements into the audit bundle.

5) Operational evidence and telemetry retention
- Default retention: 365 days; extendable per contract.
- Evidence bundle includes diagram, sample signed events, and a CSV mapping to your questionnaire fields.

Next steps: Mina will attach the questionnaire mapping and a short runbook excerpt describing emergency escrow release and rollback.

Priyom Das
Director, Applied Security
Redwood Inference

Thanks — the PDF helps clarify. A couple of clarifying questions before we route to legal/procurement:

- Rotation specifics: can Redwood support a policy where Acme forces an immediate wrap (ad-hoc rotation) and receives the signed rotation nonce within 15 minutes? We need the SLA for emergency rotations documented.
- Offline HSM support: we sometimes need air-gapped HSMs for certain zones. Can Redwood accept attestation blobs generated offline and then upload them into the control plane post-facto? If so, what format and verification steps do you require?
- Escrow: can you show a sanitized example of a notarized ceremony log (redacted operator IDs) so our audit team can see fields?

Also — we'll need a one-page runbook that describes the emergency release procedure so our on-call knows what to trigger. Can you provide that and the completed questionnaire back by EOD Tuesday PST?

Regards,
Tom Rivera

AcmeCorp

Tom / Alice —

Short answers and next steps:

- Emergency rotation SLA: Yes — we support an ad-hoc wrap with an internal target of 10 minutes for the attestation artifact generation and 15 minutes for delivery into your audit bundle when using sealed-proxy in-VPC mode. We'll include this SLA in the SOW appendix and provide a sample runbook.
- Offline HSMs: Supported. We accept attestation blobs in the industry-standard CAVP-style signed structure (ASN.1 DER wrapped, with HSM signature). Our verification process requires the HSM public attestation key (or chain) and a nonce exchange; we document the exact steps in the runbook.
- Notarized ceremony log: attaching a sanitized example and the questionnaire mapping (Attachment: acme-matrix-telemetry-map.xlsx, kms-questionnaire-filled.pdf).

1) Priyom / Mina: confirm inclusion of SLA language and attach the one-page emergency-release runbook (Mina).
